summary: Professional website for QuickRepair, a 10-minute home repair service in Mahipalpur, Delhi. Features hamburger nav menu, services grid with fixed prices (Plumber ₹499, Electrician ₹299, Fan/Cooler ₹199, AC Repair ₹479, Mechanic ₹399), WhatsApp booking integration, Become a Mechanic WhatsApp link, About/Contact sections, footer, a customer feedback/reviews section with 5-star ratings and live feedback submission, Google LocalBusiness JSON-LD schema markup, FAQ section, floating Call Now button, trust stats bar, How It Works section, performance optimizations (lazy loading, deferred backend calls, reduced initial animations), Internet Identity authentication with user registration/profile, and a private admin panel at /admin for viewing registered users and managing feedback.
architectural_notes: Business: QuickRepair — 'Quick' in yellow #FFD700, 'Repair' in orange #FF8C42
Fixed prices: Plumber ₹499, Electrician ₹299, Fan/Cooler ₹199, AC Repair ₹479, Mechanic ₹399 — DO NOT change
Service areas: Mahipalpur Extension, Mahipalpur Village, Aerocity, Vasant Kunj, Rangpuri, Nagal Dewat
Google Site Verification meta tag: <meta name="google-site-verification" content="Ce5nKYJ6ibA6FuN3CM04vXwogjB1GER3VSvSL9-Fst4" /> must be in <head> before <body>
Customer feedback: ratings and reviews submitted by visitors are stored and displayed publicly; section placed between Services and About

Google LocalBusiness JSON-LD schema in <head>: business URL https://quickrepair-84g.caffeine.xyz, logo https://quickrepair-84g.caffeine.xyz/logo.png, address Mahipalpur Delhi 110037 IN, hours Mon-Sun 08:00-20:00, emergency 24x7
Auth: Internet Identity (passkey/Google/Apple); user principal is unique ID; auto-registered on first login; profile fields: name, phone, service area
Admin panel at /admin: protected by hardcoded admin principal; shows users table + feedback table with delete capability

existing_features.title: Create a sticky header with the QuickRepair logo ('Quick' in yellow #FFD700, 'Repair' in orange #FF8C42) and a hamburger menu (☰) icon that opens a slide-in navigation drawer with an overlay backdrop. The menu must close smoothly when any option is clicked.

Implement navigation menu with five options: Home, Services, About, Contact, and Become a Mechanic. Smooth scroll to corresponding page sections for Home, Services, About, and Contact. 'Become a Mechanic' opens WhatsApp with pre-filled message: https://wa.me/8447978940?text=Hi%2C%20I%20want%20to%20become%20a%20mechanic%20at%20QuickRepair.

Build a full-viewport hero section with the tagline '10 Minute Service at Your Doorstep', a prominent call-to-action WhatsApp booking button, and a fade-in entrance animation. The hero must use the brand color palette (dark background, yellow/orange accents).

Create a services grid section displaying all 5 services with their strictly fixed prices: Plumber ₹499, Electrician ₹299, Fan/Cooler Repair ₹199, AC Repair ₹479, Mechanic (General) ₹399. Each card must have a relevant icon, subtle shadow, and a hover animation. Each card links to a WhatsApp booking message pre-filled with the service name.
Build an About section describing QuickRepair as a fast, reliable 10-minute home repair service in Mahipalpur, Delhi, emphasizing speed, professionalism, and affordability.

Build a Contact section displaying: phone number 8447978940 (as a clickable tel: link), email quickrepaironlineservices@gmail.com (as a mailto: link), service areas (Mahipalpur Extension, Mahipalpur Village, Aerocity, Vasant Kunj, Rangpuri, Nagal Dewat), and working hours (8 AM to 8 PM).

Add a footer with copyright text: '© 2024 QuickRepair. All rights reserved.' and a floating sticky WhatsApp booking button that is always visible on the bottom-right corner of the screen on all devices.

Apply a cohesive dark-themed visual design using #0d0d0d or #111111 background, #FFD700 (yellow) and #FF8C42 (orange) as primary accent colors, white body text, and a bold modern sans-serif font. Ensure all interactive elements have clear hover/active feedback, sufficient color contrast for readability, and smooth CSS transitions throughout.

Add the Google Search Console verification meta tag `<meta name="google-site-verification" content="Ce5nKYJ6ibA6FuN3CM04vXwogjB1GER3VSvSL9-Fst4" />` inside the `<head>` section of `frontend/index.html`, placed before the first `<body>` tag.

Build a FeedbackSection React component placed between the ServicesSection and AboutSection in App.tsx. The section must: (1) display pre-seeded sample reviews (at least 3) alongside any live-submitted reviews fetched from the backend via React Query; (2) show each review as a card with reviewer name, 5-star visual rating (filled stars in #FFD700), and feedback text; (3) display an aggregate average star rating and total review count prominently at the top of the section; (4) include a submission form with fields for name, star rating selector (1–5 interactive stars), and written feedback message, with a Submit button that calls the backend submitFeedback function and refreshes the list on success; (5) match the dark-themed design (#0d0d0d background, #FFD700/#FF8C42 accents, white text, smooth CSS transitions).

Inject a complete Google LocalBusiness JSON-LD structured-data script block inside the `<head>` section of `frontend/index.html`, immediately after the existing Google Search Console meta tag. The JSON-LD must include: @type 'LocalBusiness', name 'QuickRepair Mahipalpur', description '10 minute service at your doorstep. Verified mechanics, cash on delivery. Fast plumbing, electrical, AC, cooler, and general mechanic services in Mahipalpur, Delhi.', url 'https://quickrepair-84g.caffeine.xyz', telephone '+918447978940', email 'quickrepaironlineservices@gmail.com', priceRange '₹160 – ₹470', logo 'https://quickrepair-84g.caffeine.xyz/logo.png', address (streetAddress 'Mahipalpur', addressLocality 'Delhi', postalCode '110037', addressCountry 'IN'), openingHoursSpecification for Monday–Sunday 08:00–20:00 plus a second entry noting emergency 24x7 availability, areaServed listing the six localities (Mahipalpur Extension, Mahipalpur Village, Aerocity, Vasant Kunj, Rangpuri, Nagal Dewat), hasOfferCatalog with five Offer entries (Plumber ₹460 – leakage/pipe fitting/tap repair/drainage/geyser installation; Electrician ₹160 – wiring/switchboard repair/MCB/fan regulator/inverter; Fan/Cooler Repair ₹190 – ceiling fan/table fan/exhaust fan/desert cooler/air cooler; AC Repair & Service ₹470 – gas refill/general service/split AC/window AC/installation; Mechanic General ₹390 – door repair/grill work/window fittings/furniture assembly), and paymentAccepted 'Cash on Delivery'.

Create a FAQSection React component with at least 8 relevant Q&As covering pricing, booking process, response time, service areas, COD payment, and service availability. Implement accordion-style expand/collapse for each item. Match the dark-themed design (#0d0d0d background, #FFD700/#FF8C42 accents, white text). Place the FAQSection in App.tsx after the ContactSection and before the Footer.

Create a LanguagePopup React component that appears as a centered modal overlay on the first visit to the website. It must offer four language options: हिंदी (Hindi), English, বাংলা (Bengali), தமிழ் (Tamil). On selecting any option, store the preference in localStorage (key: 'qr_lang') and dismiss the popup. On subsequent visits, if a preference is stored, do not show the popup. The popup must have a dark-themed design consistent with the site (#111111 background, #FFD700 accents), a semi-transparent backdrop, and smooth fade-in/out animation.

Add a floating 'Call Now' button fixed to the bottom-right of the screen, positioned directly above the existing FloatingWhatsAppButton. The button must link to 'tel:8447978940', use a phone icon, and have styling consistent with the brand (use #FF8C42 or #FFD700 accent color). It must be visible on all screen sizes and have a hover/active state animation.

Add a TrustStatsBar React component displaying at least three trust indicators: '500+ Happy Customers', '10-Min Response', and '5★ Rated'. Place it in App.tsx immediately below the HeroSection and above the ServicesSection. Use a horizontally scrollable or flex-wrap layout on mobile. Style with dark background, #FFD700/#FF8C42 accent numbers/icons, and white text. Add a subtle fade-in-on-scroll animation.

Create a HowItWorksSection React component displaying a 3-step process: Step 1 'Book via WhatsApp', Step 2 'Mechanic Arrives in 10 Min', Step 3 'Problem Solved'. Each step must have a numbered badge, a relevant icon, a short title, and a one-line description. Connect the steps with a visual connector (arrow or line) on desktop. Place HowItWorksSection in App.tsx between the TrustStatsBar and ServicesSection. Match the dark brand theme with #FFD700/#FF8C42 accents.

Implement performance optimizations across the frontend: (1) Wrap all page sections below the fold (ServicesSection, FeedbackSection, AboutSection, ContactSection, FAQSection, HowItWorksSection) in React.lazy + Suspense with a lightweight fallback placeholder so they load after the initial paint. (2) Defer the React Query fetch for feedback data (useQueries hooks) so it does not fire on initial page load — use a short idle delay (e.g., 500ms via setTimeout or `enabled` flag tied to an idle state) before enabling the query. (3) Remove or reduce CSS keyframe animations that fire unconditionally on page load; ensure entrance animations only trigger when the element is visible via IntersectionObserver (reuse the existing useFadeIn hook pattern). (4) Add preconnect link hints in frontend/index.html for icp0.io and identity.ic0.app domains.

Rewrite the LanguagePopup component in frontend/src/components/LanguagePopup.tsx so that: (1) the initial open/closed state is determined synchronously at module evaluation time (i.e., read localStorage key 'qr_lang' before the first render using a lazy useState initializer or a module-level check), eliminating the race condition that causes the popup to flash on return visits or fail to appear on first visits; (2) the visibility state is a clear two-phase model — 'open' (fully visible) and 'closing' (fade-out animation playing) — so that clicking any language option atomically sets the chosen language in localStorage and transitions to the 'closing' phase, then unmounts the popup after the animation completes; (3) the popup is guaranteed to appear on every first visit (no 'qr_lang' in localStorage) and guaranteed NOT to appear on return visits (key present), with no intermittent behavior; (4) all four language options (हिंदी, English, বাংলা, தமிழ்) correctly write their respective value to localStorage key 'qr_lang' on click and trigger the dismiss flow; (5) the dark-themed design (#111111 background, #FFD700 accents), semi-transparent backdrop, and smooth fade-in/out CSS transition are preserved.

Delete the file frontend/src/components/LanguagePopup.tsx entirely and remove all imports, usages, and references to LanguagePopup from frontend/src/App.tsx so the language selection popup no longer appears on the site.

Add Internet Identity sign-in/sign-out UI to the Header component. When the user is not authenticated, show a 'Sign In' button styled with the brand colors (#FFD700/#FF8C42). When authenticated, show a small avatar/icon with the user's name (if registered) or a truncated principal, and a 'Sign Out' option in a dropdown or inline. Use the existing `useInternetIdentity` hook (immutable, already present) to manage auth state. The sign-in button must call the Internet Identity login flow. On successful login, if the user has no stored profile, navigate or scroll to a profile completion modal/section.

Create a ProfileModal React component (`frontend/src/components/ProfileModal.tsx`) that appears as a centered modal overlay after first login when no profile exists. It must contain a form with three fields: Full Name (text input), Phone Number (text input), and Service Area (a select or text input listing Mahipalpur Extension, Mahipalpur Village, Aerocity, Vasant Kunj, Rangpuri, Nagal Dewat). A 'Save Profile' button calls the backend `registerUser` function via the actor, then closes the modal and invalidates the React Query cache for the profile. A 'Skip for now' link dismisses the modal without saving. The modal must match the dark-themed design (#111111 background, #FFD700/#FF8C42 accents, white text, semi-transparent backdrop).

Create an AdminPage React component at `frontend/src/components/AdminPage.tsx` and add a `/admin` route in the application. The page must: (1) check if the authenticated user's principal matches the hardcoded admin principal — if not authenticated or not admin, display an 'Access Denied' message with a link back to the homepage; (2) show a 'Registered Users' table with columns: Principal (truncated), Name, Phone, Service Area, Signup Date; (3) show a 'Customer Feedback' table with columns: Reviewer Name, Rating (stars), Message, Date, and a Delete button per row; (4) the Delete button in the Feedback table calls the backend `deleteFeedback(id)` function and refreshes the feedback list; (5) the Delete button in the Users table calls `deleteUser(principal)` and refreshes the users list; (6) both tables are fetched via React Query using the authenticated actor; (7) match the dark-themed design (#0d0d0d background, #FFD700/#FF8C42 accents, white text). Add a navigation link or direct URL access at `/admin`.

Add React Query hooks to `frontend/src/hooks/useQueries.ts` for the new backend functions: (1) `useMyProfile()` — fetches the authenticated user's profile using `getMyProfile()`; (2) `useAllUsers()` — fetches all registered users using `getUsers()`, enabled only when the authenticated actor is available; (3) a mutation hook `useRegisterUser()` — calls `registerUser(name, phone, area)` on the actor and invalidates the profile query on success; (4) a mutation hook `useDeleteUser()` — calls `deleteUser(principal)` and invalidates the users list; (5) a mutation hook `useDeleteFeedback()` — calls `deleteFeedback(id)` and invalidates the feedback list. All hooks must use the actor from the existing `useActor` hook pattern already in the codebase.

Add Internet Identity sign-in/sign-out UI to the Header component (`frontend/src/components/Header.tsx`). When the user is not authenticated, show a 'Sign In' button styled with brand colors (#FFD700/#FF8C42). When authenticated, show a small avatar icon with the user's name (if a profile exists) or a truncated principal, and a 'Sign Out' option inline or in a dropdown. Use the existing `useInternetIdentity` hook to manage auth state. On successful login, if the user has no stored profile (checked via `useMyProfile`), open the ProfileModal.

Create a ProfileModal React component at `frontend/src/components/ProfileModal.tsx` that appears as a centered modal overlay after first login when no profile exists. It must contain a form with three fields: Full Name (text input), Phone Number (text input), and Service Area (a select listing: Mahipalpur Extension, Mahipalpur Village, Aerocity, Vasant Kunj, Rangpuri, Nagal Dewat). A 'Save Profile' button calls the backend `registerUser` function via the actor, then closes the modal and invalidates the React Query cache for the profile query. A 'Skip for now' link dismisses the modal without saving. The modal must match the dark-themed design (#111111 background, #FFD700/#FF8C42 accents, white text, semi-transparent backdrop).

Create an AdminPage React component at `frontend/src/components/AdminPage.tsx` and add a `/admin` route in the application (using React Router or hash-based routing consistent with existing patterns). The page must: (1) check if the authenticated user's principal matches the hardcoded admin principal — if not authenticated or not admin, display an 'Access Denied' message with a link back to the homepage; (2) show a 'Registered Users' table with columns: Principal (truncated), Name, Phone, Service Area, Signup Date; (3) show a 'Customer Feedback' table with columns: Reviewer Name, Rating (stars), Message, Date, and a Delete button per row; (4) the Delete button in the Feedback table calls the backend `deleteFeedback(id)` function and refreshes the feedback list; (5) the Delete button in the Users table calls `deleteUser(principal)` and refreshes the users list; (6) both tables are fetched via React Query using the authenticated actor; (7) match the dark-themed design (#0d0d0d background, #FFD700/#FF8C42 accents, white text).

All hooks must follow the existing `useActor` hook pattern already present in the codebase.

Nav menu options: Home, Services, About, Contact, Become a Mechanic
Hero section with tagline '10 Minute Service at Your Doorstep'
Services grid with all 5 services and fixed prices
WhatsApp booking button and Become a Mechanic WhatsApp pre-filled message link

Footer with copyright
Smooth animations, hover effects, card shadows, button feedback, responsive mobile layout
Add Google Search Console verification meta tag to <head> section
Customer feedback section between Services and About sections with 5-star ratings, sample reviews displayed, and live feedback submission stored and shown publicly

Create a Motoko backend data store to persist customer feedback submissions. Each submission must store: a reviewer name (text), a star rating (1–5), and a written feedback message (text), along with a timestamp. Expose three public functions: (1) submitFeedback(name, rating, message) to save a new review, (2) getFeedbacks() to return all stored reviews sorted newest-first, and (3) getAverageRating() to return the computed average star rating across all submissions.

Add Google LocalBusiness JSON-LD schema in <head> with full business details: name, address, phone, email, hours (Mon-Sun 8AM-8PM + 24x7 emergency), price range ₹160-₹470, logo URL, 6 service areas, 5 services with prices/descriptions, and Cash on Delivery payment method
Add FAQ section with relevant Q&As about pricing, booking, response time, service areas, and COD payment
Floating 'Call Now' button alongside the existing WhatsApp button
Trust stats bar showing e.g. '500+ Happy Customers · 10-Min Response · 5★ Rated'
How It Works 3-step section: Book → Mechanic Arrives → Problem Solved
Internet Identity login/sign-in button in header with auto-registration on first login and optional profile form (name, phone, service area)
Private admin panel at /admin showing registered users table (principal, name, phone, service area, signup date) and feedback table with delete actions, protected by hardcoded admin principal
Motoko backend: registerUser, getUsers (admin-only), deleteUser (admin-only), deleteFeedback (admin-only) functions

Extend the Motoko backend actor with user registration and admin-only functions: (1) `registerUser(name: Text, phone: Text, area: Text)` — stores a user profile keyed by the caller's principal, recording name, phone, service area, and signup timestamp; if the principal already exists, it updates the profile; (2) `getMyProfile()` — returns the caller's own profile if it exists; (3) `getUsers()` — admin-only, returns all registered user profiles as an array; (4) `deleteUser(p: Principal)` — admin-only, removes the user profile for the given principal; (5) `deleteFeedback(id: Nat)` — admin-only, removes the feedback entry with the matching id (add an id field to stored feedback if not present). Admin-only functions must check that the caller's principal matches a hardcoded admin principal constant defined at the top of the actor. The admin principal must be set to `"2vxsx-fae"` as a placeholder — add a comment instructing the deployer to replace it with their actual Internet Identity principal.

Extend the Motoko backend actor in backend/main.mo with user registration and admin-only functions: (1) `registerUser(name: Text, phone: Text, area: Text)` — stores a user profile keyed by the caller's principal, recording name, phone, service area, and signup timestamp; if the principal already exists, update the profile; (2) `getMyProfile()` — returns the caller's own profile as an optional record; (3) `getUsers()` — admin-only, returns all registered user profiles as an array; (4) `deleteUser(p: Principal)` — admin-only, removes the user profile for the given principal; (5) `deleteFeedback(id: Nat)` — admin-only, removes the feedback entry with the matching id (add an id field to stored feedback if not already present). Admin-only functions must check that the caller's principal matches a hardcoded admin principal constant defined at the top of the actor, initially set to `"2vxsx-fae"` with a comment instructing the deployer to replace it with their actual Internet Identity principal.
